question.text: A PM manages a Rs. 200 crore portfolio with Modified Duration 4.5. Rates rise by 75 bps. Approximate price impact:

explanation.text: The Logic: Percent price change ≈ −Modified Duration × decimal change in market interest rates. Δ Value ≈ −4.5 × 0.0075 × Rs. 200 cr = −Rs. 6.75 cr, i.e. a Rs. 6.75 cr loss. The Trap: Rs. 3.375 cr halves the duration application; Rs. 9.00 cr overstates it; a 'gain' has the wrong sign for a rate rise. Note: Modified duration is the standard bond-portfolio sensitivity measure to interest-rate changes.
